mechanism_narrative: Persistently low WORKPLACES mobility depresses weekday trip chains and incidental shopping, so RETAIL_REC stays lower over the next four weeks than over the prior four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES is around -30% in all four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES remains near its current depressed level, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A further week-on-week drop in TRANSIT below its current level signals weaker footfall access to shopping districts, which translates into lower RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -33% after already being below -30% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -30.4 to -34.1 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses below -33% and RETAIL_REC does not decline further within the next 2 weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility rises while GROCERY_PHARM is flat or falling, households are substituting toward at-home activity and fewer discretionary errands, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is rising while GROCERY_PHARM is near zero
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL keeps rising but RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the last 4 weeks, or if GROCERY_PHARM rises materially with it, the claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility from a negative weekly trough indicates improving weather-driven outing intensity, which spills over into more retail visits and raises RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns upward from below -5% week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -10.6 then improved to -4.7
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds above -5% and RETAIL_REC does not improve in the following week, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates renewed restrictions or remote-work tightening, and that combined shock reduces retail demand over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain at least 2 points below their previous week's means
evidence_refs: fact:both series are already near their lowest observed levels in the snapshot
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay depressed yet RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM acts as an errand-intensity signal: households making more essential trips also consolidate discretionary shopping, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above its previous 2-week average after a negative or flat run
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improves from -4.9 to -2.1 in the snapshot
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises above its prior 2-week average and RETAIL_REC does not increase within 2 weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while WORKPLACES stays deeply negative, time spent near home replaces shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC declines further over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is above baseline while WORKPLACES is near -30%
failure_condition: If high RESIDENTIAL and low WORKPLACES persist but RETAIL_REC does not underperform its last-4-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A regime with transit recovery but still-subdued workplaces signals partial reopening: commuting resumes before office occupancy fully normalizes, and retail benefits after a short lag.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES stays below -25%
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is falling now, so the trigger is currently absent
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises for two weeks with WORKPLACES still below -25% and RETAIL_REC does not improve in the next week, the hypothesis fails.
